# gh-1450: [GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)

## Description

[WIP][GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)

## Goal — the authorization URL is always visible and browser launch is always optional (v1)

One sentence: **OAuth/SSO login in fa becomes a flow where the full authorization URL is printed in every outcome and the automatic browser launch can be declined** — not a flow that hides the URL exactly when the launch command reports success.

Today all browser-driven login flows print the authorization URL only in the `openBrowser`-returned-false branch; in the success branch they print "browser opened" and nothing else. `openBrowser()` returns true merely because a launch command exited 0 — which says nothing about which browser, which profile, or whether a browser opened at all (SSH, headless, wrong default profile). A user for whom the default browser is the wrong destination gets a silent wait and a timeout that never reveals the URL. The fix is uniform: the URL is a first-class output line in BOTH branches, launch is skippable by flag, env, and headless auto-detect, and the timeout message carries the URL as a last-chance rescue.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the success branch is the happy path and needs no URL." That holds only when the default browser is the right destination. The incident shows the launch succeeding (exit 0) while being useless to the user — the URL was needed most precisely in the success branch.
- **Retracted:** "printing the URL always is redundant noise for interactive users." One extra status line per login is negligible; its absence is unrecoverable when the launch is wrong. Redundancy here is the safety property, not clutter.
- **Retracted (scope):** "fix CodeMie only — that is where the incident happened." OpenRouter and ChatGPT interactive flows share the identical branch shape through the same imported `openBrowser`; fixing one mechanism class means fixing all of them (AIIN is the fourth family member — see Capability surface).

## Incident (owner, 2026-10-09 — test data)

CodeMie SSO login in fa (`/provider` flow → `runCodeMieSsoCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:161`). fa opened the auth link in the DEFAULT browser. The owner cannot authorize there (wrong browser/profile context), and the full URL was never printed, so he could not open it in the right browser himself. The flow waited and timed out. Owner quote: "оно открывает ссылку в дефолт браузере, а мне там не надо! я там не могу авторизовать, а ссылку оно полную не даёт".

Mechanism chain (each link pinned below):
(a) flow builds the URL and calls `openBrowserFn(ssoUrl)`;
(b) `openBrowser` shells out to `open`/`xdg-open`/`start` and reports "true when the launch command was invoked (not whether the browser actually opened)" — SSH/X-less sessions and wrong-default-profile sessions still report true;
(c) the true branch prints only "browser opened" — the URL is hidden exactly when the launch was attempted;
(d) the wait loop runs 5 minutes of "still waiting" statuses, then the timeout path returns without ever printing the URL — no self-rescue at any point.

Amplification: the success-branch design was self-confirming — every local, single-profile test session saw the browser open and the flow complete, so the missing URL line never surfaced as a failure. It survived until a multi-context user (remote machine / non-default browser profile) hit it, and even then the timeout made the failure look like a provider problem rather than a harness problem.

## Architecture (pinned facts, re-verified against the working tree)

The three interactive flows share one shape — an injectable `openBrowserFn` seam defaulting to the shared `openBrowser`, a branch on its boolean, and a timeout path:

```
runXxxCliFlow
  ├─ build <authUrl>  (callback port + state embedded; token never part of the URL)
  ├─ openBrowserFn(authUrl) ──true──▶ onStatus('browser opened; …')   ← URL HIDDEN
  │                        └─false─▶ onStatus('open this URL manually: $url')  ← only rescue line today
  ├─ wait for localhost callback (5 min, periodic 'still waiting')
  └─ timeout ─▶ onStatus('no … received (timeout or cancelled)')      ← URL HIDDEN
```

- `lib/src/cli/codemie_sso_server.dart:75` `runCodeMieSsoCliFlow` starts the callback server, builds `ssoUrl` (`:82`), branches at `:84-89`: success prints only `'browser opened; complete the CodeMie sign-in'` (`:85`); failure prints `'could not open browser automatically'` (`:87`) and `'open this URL manually: $ssoUrl'` (`:88`). Wait loop `:90-107`: `const wait = Duration(minutes: 5)` (`:98`), periodic "still waiting" every 15 s (`:99-101`), `server.waitForToken().timeout(wait)` (`:103`). Timeout branch `:108-110` prints `'no SSO callback received (timeout or cancelled)'` — no URL.
- `lib/src/cli/openrouter_oauth_server.dart:157-178` `openBrowser` (doc `:152-156`): `open` (macOS) / `xdg-open` (Linux) / `start` (Windows), returns `result.exitCode == 0`; unsupported platform and thrown launch errors return false. Doc comment admits: "Returns true when the launch command was invoked (not whether the browser actually opened)."
- `lib/src/cli/openrouter_oauth_server.dart:185` `runOpenRouterOAuthCliFlow`: `opened = await openBrowserFn(authUrl.toString())` at `:210`; success `:211-212` prints only `'browser opened; complete authorization on the OpenRouter page'`; failure `:213-216` prints the manual-URL line. Timeout `:218-221` — no URL.
- `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_oauth_server.dart:9` imports `openBrowser` from `openrouter_oauth_server.dart`; `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow` (`:149`) takes `openBrowserFn = openBrowser` (`:151`), branches at `:172-177` (success `:173` `'browser opened; complete authorization with ChatGPT'` hides the URL; failure `:176` prints it). Timeout `:178-181` — no URL.
- Fourth family member, same shape: `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart` imports `openBrowser` at `:21`; `runAiinConnectCliFlow` (`:204`) takes `openBrowserFn` (`:206`); the branch lives at `:484-488` (success `:485` `'browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page'`, failure `:488` manual-URL line).
- Call sites: `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:145` (OpenRouter via `/provider`), `:161` (CodeMie SSO via `_mintCodeMieSsoCookie`, `:157`), `:1086` (OpenRouter re-login), `:1250-1298` (ChatGPT: `/provider chatgpt oauth [headless]` → `_handleChatGptOAuthCommand` `:1246` → `_runChatGptOAuthCommand` `:1257`, headless variant dispatched at `:1296`, interactive `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow` at `:1298`), `:1561` (CodeMie SSO recovery via `_handleCodeMieSsoCommand`, `:1551`).
- Precedent IN REPO that the target shape is not foreign: `_runChatGptHeadlessOAuth` (`lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:1322`) is a no-browser OAuth flow — it prints the instruction and the full URL (`io.writeln(authUrl.toString())`, `:1344`), then asks the user to paste the redirect URL. The card's core behavior already exists in the codebase for exactly one flow.
- No opt-out exists today: no `--no-browser` flag and no `FA_NO_BROWSER` env var anywhere in `lib/`, `bin/`, or `test/`. The only related env var is `FA_NO_FORMAT` (rendering only; `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart:280`, `lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart:1322`) — unrelated to browser launch.
- URL contents (threat-model input): CodeMie's URL is `<org base>/v1/auth/login/<port>` (`lib/src/providers/codemie_sso.dart:38-39`) — the localhost callback port is embedded; the token arrives later via the redirect to `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...` (`:36-37`) and is therefore never part of the printed URL. OpenRouter/ChatGPT URLs carry PKCE challenge + `state` + redirect URI.

**Positive/negative tests for the load-bearing fact** ("true ≠ opened"):
- Positive: with `openBrowserFn` stubbed to `async (u) => true`, the success branch must STILL print the full URL (this is the fix; today it does not — `test/cli/codemie_sso_server_test.dart:142` pins the old behavior).
- Negative: with the stub returning false, the URL line is…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1464
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1464
- **Title**: gh-1450 [GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1450` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +1602
- **Deletions**: -187
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T22:50:43Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T23:59:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1450
### What changed
Every CLI OAuth/SSO flow (OpenRouter, ChatGPT/Codex, CodeMie SSO, AIIN connect) now always prints a consistent, greppable `authorization URL: <url>` line, and a new `--no-browser` flag (plus a truthy `FA_NO_BROWSER` env var and a headless/remote auto-detect) skips the automatic browser launch — the URL stays on screen so the user can copy it into any browser and paste/redirect the callback back.

### Key decisions
- One shared launch step, `openAuthUrlWithStatus`, used by all four flows: prints skip/opened/could-not-open, then ALWAYS the URL line (also on timeout/failure — last-chance rescue) so the URL is never suppressed.
- New `shouldLaunchBrowser` policy in `openrouter_oauth_server.dart`: explicit `--no-browser` flag > `FA_NO_BROWSER` env > headless auto-detect (`TERM=dumb`, no `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` on Linux, SSH without display, non-TTY stdout).
- Flag threaded through `provider_commands` / per-provider command handlers into `runXxxCliFlow(shouldOpenBrowserFn: …)`; each flow keeps its `openBrowserFn` seam.
- AIIN connect now rides the configured `modelsHttpClient`, so the flow's exchange/key calls are testable without network.
- Command-layer end-to-end coverage in `agent_cli_oauth_no_browser_test.dart`: tests play the browser (read the printed URL, fire the real loopback callback) for OpenRouter, CodeMie, and AIIN; ChatGPT stays flow-test-only (its callback server binds pinned ports 1455/1457).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/agent_cli_oauth_no_browser_test.dart
dart test test/cli/browser_launch_policy_test.dart test/cli/openrouter_oauth_server_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_oauth_server_test.dart test/cli/codemie_sso_server_test.dart test/cli/aiin_connect_server_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Flow shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CMD["/provider … oauth|sso|connect --no-browser"] --> FLOW["runXxxCliFlow"]
  FLOOR["shouldLaunchBrowser: flag > FA_NO_BROWSER > headless detect"] --> FLOW
  FLOW -->|"false"| SKIP["prints: browser launch skipped"]
  FLOW -->|"true"| OPEN["openBrowserFn(url)"]
  SKIP --> URL
  OPEN --> URL["prints: authorization URL: <url>"]
  URL --> CB["loopback callback (user-driven)"]
  CB --> DONE["exchange / cookies → provider saved"]
```

# gh-1450: [GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)

## Description

[WIP][GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)

## Goal — the authorization URL is always visible and browser launch is always optional (v1)

One sentence: **OAuth/SSO login in fa becomes a flow where the full authorization URL is printed in every outcome and the automatic browser launch can be declined** — not a flow that hides the URL exactly when the launch command reports success.

Today all browser-driven login flows print the authorization URL only in the `openBrowser`-returned-false branch; in the success branch they print "browser opened" and nothing else. `openBrowser()` returns true merely because a launch command exited 0 — which says nothing about which browser, which profile, or whether a browser opened at all (SSH, headless, wrong default profile). A user for whom the default browser is the wrong destination gets a silent wait and a timeout that never reveals the URL. The fix is uniform: the URL is a first-class output line in BOTH branches, launch is skippable by flag, env, and headless auto-detect, and the timeout message carries the URL as a last-chance rescue.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the success branch is the happy path and needs no URL." That holds only when the default browser is the right destination. The incident shows the launch succeeding (exit 0) while being useless to the user — the URL was needed most precisely in the success branch.
- **Retracted:** "printing the URL always is redundant noise for interactive users." One extra status line per login is negligible; its absence is unrecoverable when the launch is wrong. Redundancy here is the safety property, not clutter.
- **Retracted (scope):** "fix CodeMie only — that is where the incident happened." OpenRouter and ChatGPT interactive flows share the identical branch shape through the same imported `openBrowser`; fixing one mechanism class means fixing all of them (AIIN is the fourth family member — see Capability surface).

## Incident (owner, 2026-10-09 — test data)

CodeMie SSO login in fa (`/provider` flow → `runCodeMieSsoCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:161`). fa opened the auth link in the DEFAULT browser. The owner cannot authorize there (wrong browser/profile context), and the full URL was never printed, so he could not open it in the right browser himself. The flow waited and timed out. Owner quote: "оно открывает ссылку в дефолт браузере, а мне там не надо! я там не могу авторизовать, а ссылку оно полную не даёт".

Mechanism chain (each link pinned below):
(a) flow builds the URL and calls `openBrowserFn(ssoUrl)`;
(b) `openBrowser` shells out to `open`/`xdg-open`/`start` and reports "true when the launch command was invoked (not whether the browser actually opened)" — SSH/X-less sessions and wrong-default-profile sessions still report true;
(c) the true branch prints only "browser opened" — the URL is hidden exactly when the launch was attempted;
(d) the wait loop runs 5 minutes of "still waiting" statuses, then the timeout path returns without ever printing the URL — no self-rescue at any point.

Amplification: the success-branch design was self-confirming — every local, single-profile test session saw the browser open and the flow complete, so the missing URL line never surfaced as a failure. It survived until a multi-context user (remote machine / non-default browser profile) hit it, and even then the timeout made the failure look like a provider problem rather than a harness problem.

## Architecture (pinned facts, re-verified against the working tree)

The three interactive flows share one shape — an injectable `openBrowserFn` seam defaulting to the shared `openBrowser`, a branch on its boolean, and a timeout path:

```
runXxxCliFlow
  ├─ build <authUrl>  (callback port + state embedded; token never part of the URL)
  ├─ openBrowserFn(authUrl) ──true──▶ onStatus('browser opened; …')   ← URL HIDDEN
  │                        └─false─▶ onStatus('open this URL manually: $url')  ← only rescue line today
  ├─ wait for localhost callback (5 min, periodic 'still waiting')
  └─ timeout ─▶ onStatus('no … received (timeout or cancelled)')      ← URL HIDDEN
```

- `lib/src/cli/codemie_sso_server.dart:75` `runCodeMieSsoCliFlow` starts the callback server, builds `ssoUrl` (`:82`), branches at `:84-89`: success prints only `'browser opened; complete the CodeMie sign-in'` (`:85`); failure prints `'could not open browser automatically'` (`:87`) and `'open this URL manually: $ssoUrl'` (`:88`). Wait loop `:90-107`: `const wait = Duration(minutes: 5)` (`:98`), periodic "still waiting" every 15 s (`:99-101`), `server.waitForToken().timeout(wait)` (`:103`). Timeout branch `:108-110` prints `'no SSO callback received (timeout or cancelled)'` — no URL.
- `lib/src/cli/openrouter_oauth_server.dart:157-178` `openBrowser` (doc `:152-156`): `open` (macOS) / `xdg-open` (Linux) / `start` (Windows), returns `result.exitCode == 0`; unsupported platform and thrown launch errors return false. Doc comment admits: "Returns true when the launch command was invoked (not whether the browser actually opened)."
- `lib/src/cli/openrouter_oauth_server.dart:185` `runOpenRouterOAuthCliFlow`: `opened = await openBrowserFn(authUrl.toString())` at `:210`; success `:211-212` prints only `'browser opened; complete authorization on the OpenRouter page'`; failure `:213-216` prints the manual-URL line. Timeout `:218-221` — no URL.
- `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_oauth_server.dart:9` imports `openBrowser` from `openrouter_oauth_server.dart`; `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow` (`:149`) takes `openBrowserFn = openBrowser` (`:151`), branches at `:172-177` (success `:173` `'browser opened; complete authorization with ChatGPT'` hides the URL; failure `:176` prints it). Timeout `:178-181` — no URL.
- Fourth family member, same shape: `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart` imports `openBrowser` at `:21`; `runAiinConnectCliFlow` (`:204`) takes `openBrowserFn` (`:206`); the branch lives at `:484-488` (success `:485` `'browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page'`, failure `:488` manual-URL line).
- Call sites: `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:145` (OpenRouter via `/provider`), `:161` (CodeMie SSO via `_mintCodeMieSsoCookie`, `:157`), `:1086` (OpenRouter re-login), `:1250-1298` (ChatGPT: `/provider chatgpt oauth [headless]` → `_handleChatGptOAuthCommand` `:1246` → `_runChatGptOAuthCommand` `:1257`, headless variant dispatched at `:1296`, interactive `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow` at `:1298`), `:1561` (CodeMie SSO recovery via `_handleCodeMieSsoCommand`, `:1551`).
- Precedent IN REPO that the target shape is not foreign: `_runChatGptHeadlessOAuth` (`lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:1322`) is a no-browser OAuth flow — it prints the instruction and the full URL (`io.writeln(authUrl.toString())`, `:1344`), then asks the user to paste the redirect URL. The card's core behavior already exists in the codebase for exactly one flow.
- No opt-out exists today: no `--no-browser` flag and no `FA_NO_BROWSER` env var anywhere in `lib/`, `bin/`, or `test/`. The only related env var is `FA_NO_FORMAT` (rendering only; `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart:280`, `lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart:1322`) — unrelated to browser launch.
- URL contents (threat-model input): CodeMie's URL is `<org base>/v1/auth/login/<port>` (`lib/src/providers/codemie_sso.dart:38-39`) — the localhost callback port is embedded; the token arrives later via the redirect to `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...` (`:36-37`) and is therefore never part of the printed URL. OpenRouter/ChatGPT URLs carry PKCE challenge + `state` + redirect URI.

**Positive/negative tests for the load-bearing fact** ("true ≠ opened"):
- Positive: with `openBrowserFn` stubbed to `async (u) => true`, the success branch must STILL print the full URL (this is the fix; today it does not — `test/cli/codemie_sso_server_test.dart:142` pins the old behavior).
- Negative: with the stub returning false, the URL line is…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

- **Title**: gh-1450 [GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1450` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +1602
- **Deletions**: -187
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T22:50:43Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T23:59:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1450
### What changed
Every CLI OAuth/SSO flow (OpenRouter, ChatGPT/Codex, CodeMie SSO, AIIN connect) now always prints a consistent, greppable `authorization URL: <url>` line, and a new `--no-browser` flag (plus a truthy `FA_NO_BROWSER` env var and a headless/remote auto-detect) skips the automatic browser launch — the URL stays on screen so the user can copy it into any browser and paste/redirect the callback back.

### Key decisions
- One shared launch step, `openAuthUrlWithStatus`, used by all four flows: prints skip/opened/could-not-open, then ALWAYS the URL line (also on timeout/failure — last-chance rescue) so the URL is never suppressed.
- New `shouldLaunchBrowser` policy in `openrouter_oauth_server.dart`: explicit `--no-browser` flag > `FA_NO_BROWSER` env > headless auto-detect (`TERM=dumb`, no `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` on Linux, SSH without display, non-TTY stdout).
- Flag threaded through `provider_commands` / per-provider command handlers into `runXxxCliFlow(shouldOpenBrowserFn: …)`; each flow keeps its `openBrowserFn` seam.
- AIIN connect now rides the configured `modelsHttpClient`, so the flow's exchange/key calls are testable without network.
- Command-layer end-to-end coverage in `agent_cli_oauth_no_browser_test.dart`: tests play the browser (read the printed URL, fire the real loopback callback) for OpenRouter, CodeMie, and AIIN; ChatGPT stays flow-test-only (its callback server binds pinned ports 1455/1457).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/agent_cli_oauth_no_browser_test.dart
dart test test/cli/browser_launch_policy_test.dart test/cli/openrouter_oauth_server_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_oauth_server_test.dart test/cli/codemie_sso_server_test.dart test/cli/aiin_connect_server_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Flow shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CMD["/provider … oauth|sso|connect --no-browser"] --> FLOW["runXxxCliFlow"]
  FLOOR["shouldLaunchBrowser: flag > FA_NO_BROWSER > headless detect"] --> FLOW
  FLOW -->|"false"| SKIP["prints: browser launch skipped"]
  FLOW -->|"true"| OPEN["openBrowserFn(url)"]
  SKIP --> URL
  OPEN --> URL["prints: authorization URL: <url>"]
  URL --> CB["loopback callback (user-driven)"]
  CB --> DONE["exchange / cookies → provider saved"]
```

</details>

# gh-1450: [GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)

## Description

[WIP][GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)

## Goal — the authorization URL is always visible and browser launch is always optional (v1)

One sentence: **OAuth/SSO login in fa becomes a flow where the full authorization URL is printed in every outcome and the automatic browser launch can be declined** — not a flow that hides the URL exactly when the launch command reports success.

Today all browser-driven login flows print the authorization URL only in the `openBrowser`-returned-false branch; in the success branch they print "browser opened" and nothing else. `openBrowser()` returns true merely because a launch command exited 0 — which says nothing about which browser, which profile, or whether a browser opened at all (SSH, headless, wrong default profile). A user for whom the default browser is the wrong destination gets a silent wait and a timeout that never reveals the URL. The fix is uniform: the URL is a first-class output line in BOTH branches, launch is skippable by flag, env, and headless auto-detect, and the timeout message carries the URL as a last-chance rescue.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the success branch is the happy path and needs no URL." That holds only when the default browser is the right destination. The incident shows the launch succeeding (exit 0) while being useless to the user — the URL was needed most precisely in the success branch.
- **Retracted:** "printing the URL always is redundant noise for interactive users." One extra status line per login is negligible; its absence is unrecoverable when the launch is wrong. Redundancy here is the safety property, not clutter.
- **Retracted (scope):** "fix CodeMie only — that is where the incident happened." OpenRouter and ChatGPT interactive flows share the identical branch shape through the same imported `openBrowser`; fixing one mechanism class means fixing all of them (AIIN is the fourth family member — see Capability surface).

## Incident (owner, 2026-10-09 — test data)

CodeMie SSO login in fa (`/provider` flow → `runCodeMieSsoCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:161`). fa opened the auth link in the DEFAULT browser. The owner cannot authorize there (wrong browser/profile context), and the full URL was never printed, so he could not open it in the right browser himself. The flow waited and timed out. Owner quote: "оно открывает ссылку в дефолт браузере, а мне там не надо! я там не могу авторизовать, а ссылку оно полную не даёт".

Mechanism chain (each link pinned below):
(a) flow builds the URL and calls `openBrowserFn(ssoUrl)`;
(b) `openBrowser` shells out to `open`/`xdg-open`/`start` and reports "true when the launch command was invoked (not whether the browser actually opened)" — SSH/X-less sessions and wrong-default-profile sessions still report true;
(c) the true branch prints only "browser opened" — the URL is hidden exactly when the launch was attempted;
(d) the wait loop runs 5 minutes of "still waiting" statuses, then the timeout path returns without ever printing the URL — no self-rescue at any point.

Amplification: the success-branch design was self-confirming — every local, single-profile test session saw the browser open and the flow complete, so the missing URL line never surfaced as a failure. It survived until a multi-context user (remote machine / non-default browser profile) hit it, and even then the timeout made the failure look like a provider problem rather than a harness problem.

## Architecture (pinned facts, re-verified against the working tree)

The three interactive flows share one shape — an injectable `openBrowserFn` seam defaulting to the shared `openBrowser`, a branch on its boolean, and a timeout path:

```
runXxxCliFlow
  ├─ build <authUrl>  (callback port + state embedded; token never part of the URL)
  ├─ openBrowserFn(authUrl) ──true──▶ onStatus('browser opened; …')   ← URL HIDDEN
  │                        └─false─▶ onStatus('open this URL manually: $url')  ← only rescue line today
  ├─ wait for localhost callback (5 min, periodic 'still waiting')
  └─ timeout ─▶ onStatus('no … received (timeout or cancelled)')      ← URL HIDDEN
```

- `lib/src/cli/codemie_sso_server.dart:75` `runCodeMieSsoCliFlow` starts the callback server, builds `ssoUrl` (`:82`), branches at `:84-89`: success prints only `'browser opened; complete the CodeMie sign-in'` (`:85`); failure prints `'could not open browser automatically'` (`:87`) and `'open this URL manually: $ssoUrl'` (`:88`). Wait loop `:90-107`: `const wait = Duration(minutes: 5)` (`:98`), periodic "still waiting" every 15 s (`:99-101`), `server.waitForToken().timeout(wait)` (`:103`). Timeout branch `:108-110` prints `'no SSO callback received (timeout or cancelled)'` — no URL.
- `lib/src/cli/openrouter_oauth_server.dart:157-178` `openBrowser` (doc `:152-156`): `open` (macOS) / `xdg-open` (Linux) / `start` (Windows), returns `result.exitCode == 0`; unsupported platform and thrown launch errors return false. Doc comment admits: "Returns true when the launch command was invoked (not whether the browser actually opened)."
- `lib/src/cli/openrouter_oauth_server.dart:185` `runOpenRouterOAuthCliFlow`: `opened = await openBrowserFn(authUrl.toString())` at `:210`; success `:211-212` prints only `'browser opened; complete authorization on the OpenRouter page'`; failure `:213-216` prints the manual-URL line. Timeout `:218-221` — no URL.
- `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_oauth_server.dart:9` imports `openBrowser` from `openrouter_oauth_server.dart`; `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow` (`:149`) takes `openBrowserFn = openBrowser` (`:151`), branches at `:172-177` (success `:173` `'browser opened; complete authorization with ChatGPT'` hides the URL; failure `:176` prints it). Timeout `:178-181` — no URL.
- Fourth family member, same shape: `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart` imports `openBrowser` at `:21`; `runAiinConnectCliFlow` (`:204`) takes `openBrowserFn` (`:206`); the branch lives at `:484-488` (success `:485` `'browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page'`, failure `:488` manual-URL line).
- Call sites: `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:145` (OpenRouter via `/provider`), `:161` (CodeMie SSO via `_mintCodeMieSsoCookie`, `:157`), `:1086` (OpenRouter re-login), `:1250-1298` (ChatGPT: `/provider chatgpt oauth [headless]` → `_handleChatGptOAuthCommand` `:1246` → `_runChatGptOAuthCommand` `:1257`, headless variant dispatched at `:1296`, interactive `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow` at `:1298`), `:1561` (CodeMie SSO recovery via `_handleCodeMieSsoCommand`, `:1551`).
- Precedent IN REPO that the target shape is not foreign: `_runChatGptHeadlessOAuth` (`lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:1322`) is a no-browser OAuth flow — it prints the instruction and the full URL (`io.writeln(authUrl.toString())`, `:1344`), then asks the user to paste the redirect URL. The card's core behavior already exists in the codebase for exactly one flow.
- No opt-out exists today: no `--no-browser` flag and no `FA_NO_BROWSER` env var anywhere in `lib/`, `bin/`, or `test/`. The only related env var is `FA_NO_FORMAT` (rendering only; `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart:280`, `lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart:1322`) — unrelated to browser launch.
- URL contents (threat-model input): CodeMie's URL is `<org base>/v1/auth/login/<port>` (`lib/src/providers/codemie_sso.dart:38-39`) — the localhost callback port is embedded; the token arrives later via the redirect to `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...` (`:36-37`) and is therefore never part of the printed URL. OpenRouter/ChatGPT URLs carry PKCE challenge + `state` + redirect URI.

**Positive/negative tests for the load-bearing fact** ("true ≠ opened"):

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

- **PR #**: 1464

- **Title**: gh-1450 [GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1450` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +1602
- **Deletions**: -187
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T22:50:43Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T23:59:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1450
### What changed
Every CLI OAuth/SSO flow (OpenRouter, ChatGPT/Codex, CodeMie SSO, AIIN connect) now always prints a consistent, greppable `authorization URL: <url>` line, and a new `--no-browser` flag (plus a truthy `FA_NO_BROWSER` env var and a headless/remote auto-detect) skips the automatic browser launch — the URL stays on screen so the user can copy it into any browser and paste/redirect the callback back.

### Key decisions
- One shared launch step, `openAuthUrlWithStatus`, used by all four flows: prints skip/opened/could-not-open, then ALWAYS the URL line (also on timeout/failure — last-chance rescue) so the URL is never suppressed.
- New `shouldLaunchBrowser` policy in `openrouter_oauth_server.dart`: explicit `--no-browser` flag > `FA_NO_BROWSER` env > headless auto-detect (`TERM=dumb`, no `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` on Linux, SSH without display, non-TTY stdout).
- Flag threaded through `provider_commands` / per-provider command handlers into `runXxxCliFlow(shouldOpenBrowserFn: …)`; each flow keeps its `openBrowserFn` seam.
- AIIN connect now rides the configured `modelsHttpClient`, so the flow's exchange/key calls are testable without network.
- Command-layer end-to-end coverage in `agent_cli_oauth_no_browser_test.dart`: tests play the browser (read the printed URL, fire the real loopback callback) for OpenRouter, CodeMie, and AIIN; ChatGPT stays flow-test-only (its callback server binds pinned ports 1455/1457).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/agent_cli_oauth_no_browser_test.dart
dart test test/cli/browser_launch_policy_test.dart test/cli/openrouter_oauth_server_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_oauth_server_test.dart test/cli/codemie_sso_server_test.dart test/cli/aiin_connect_server_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Flow shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CMD["/provider … oauth|sso|connect --no-browser"] --> FLOW["runXxxCliFlow"]
  FLOOR["shouldLaunchBrowser: flag > FA_NO_BROWSER > headless detect"] --> FLOW
  FLOW -->|"false"| SKIP["prints: browser launch skipped"]
  FLOW -->|"true"| OPEN["openBrowserFn(url)"]
  SKIP --> URL
  OPEN --> URL["prints: authorization URL: <url>"]
  URL --> CB["loopback callback (user-driven)"]
  CB --> DONE["exchange / cookies → provider saved"]
```

</details>

# gh-1450: [GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)

## Description

[WIP][GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)

## Goal — the authorization URL is always visible and browser launch is always optional (v1)

One sentence: **OAuth/SSO login in fa becomes a flow where the full authorization URL is printed in every outcome and the automatic browser launch can be declined** — not a flow that hides the URL exactly when the launch command reports success.

Today all browser-driven login flows print the authorization URL only in the `openBrowser`-returned-false branch; in the success branch they print "browser opened" and nothing else. `openBrowser()` returns true merely because a launch command exited 0 — which says nothing about which browser, which profile, or whether a browser opened at all (SSH, headless, wrong default profile). A user for whom the default browser is the wrong destination gets a silent wait and a timeout that never reveals the URL. The fix is uniform: the URL is a first-class output line in BOTH branches, launch is skippable by flag, env, and headless auto-detect, and the timeout message carries the URL as a last-chance rescue.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the success branch is the happy path and needs no URL." That holds only when the default browser is the right destination. The incident shows the launch succeeding (exit 0) while being useless to the user — the URL was needed most precisely in the success branch.
- **Retracted:** "printing the URL always is redundant noise for interactive users." One extra status line per login is negligible; its absence is unrecoverable when the launch is wrong. Redundancy here is the safety property, not clutter.
- **Retracted (scope):** "fix CodeMie only — that is where the incident happened." OpenRouter and ChatGPT interactive flows share the identical branch shape through the same imported `openBrowser`; fixing one mechanism class means fixing all of them (AIIN is the fourth family member — see Capability surface).

## Incident (owner, 2026-10-09 — test data)

CodeMie SSO login in fa (`/provider` flow → `runCodeMieSsoCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:161`). fa opened the auth link in the DEFAULT browser. The owner cannot authorize there (wrong browser/profile context), and the full URL was never printed, so he could not open it in the right browser himself. The flow waited and timed out. Owner quote: "оно открывает ссылку в дефолт браузере, а мне там не надо! я там не могу авторизовать, а ссылку оно полную не даёт".

Mechanism chain (each link pinned below):
(a) flow builds the URL and calls `openBrowserFn(ssoUrl)`;
(b) `openBrowser` shells out to `open`/`xdg-open`/`start` and reports "true when the launch command was invoked (not whether the browser actually opened)" — SSH/X-less sessions and wrong-default-profile sessions still report true;
(c) the true branch prints only "browser opened" — the URL is hidden exactly when the launch was attempted;
(d) the wait loop runs 5 minutes of "still waiting" statuses, then the timeout path returns without ever printing the URL — no self-rescue at any point.

Amplification: the success-branch design was self-confirming — every local, single-profile test session saw the browser open and the flow complete, so the missing URL line never surfaced as a failure. It survived until a multi-context user (remote machine / non-default browser profile) hit it, and even then the timeout made the failure look like a provider problem rather than a harness problem.

## Architecture (pinned facts, re-verified against the working tree)

The three interactive flows share one shape — an injectable `openBrowserFn` seam defaulting to the shared `openBrowser`, a branch on its boolean, and a timeout path:

```
runXxxCliFlow
  ├─ build <authUrl>  (callback port + state embedded; token never part of the URL)
  ├─ openBrowserFn(authUrl) ──true──▶ onStatus('browser opened; …')   ← URL HIDDEN
  │                        └─false─▶ onStatus('open this URL manually: $url')  ← only rescue line today
  ├─ wait for localhost callback (5 min, periodic 'still waiting')
  └─ timeout ─▶ onStatus('no … received (timeout or cancelled)')      ← URL HIDDEN
```

- `lib/src/cli/codemie_sso_server.dart:75` `runCodeMieSsoCliFlow` starts the callback server, builds `ssoUrl` (`:82`), branches at `:84-89`: success prints only `'browser opened; complete the CodeMie sign-in'` (`:85`); failure prints `'could not open browser automatically'` (`:87`) and `'open this URL manually: $ssoUrl'` (`:88`). Wait loop `:90-107`: `const wait = Duration(minutes: 5)` (`:98`), periodic "still waiting" every 15 s (`:99-101`), `server.waitForToken().timeout(wait)` (`:103`). Timeout branch `:108-110` prints `'no SSO callback received (timeout or cancelled)'` — no URL.
- `lib/src/cli/openrouter_oauth_server.dart:157-178` `openBrowser` (doc `:152-156`): `open` (macOS) / `xdg-open` (Linux) / `start` (Windows), returns `result.exitCode == 0`; unsupported platform and thrown launch errors return false. Doc comment admits: "Returns true when the launch command was invoked (not whether the browser actually opened)."
- `lib/src/cli/openrouter_oauth_server.dart:185` `runOpenRouterOAuthCliFlow`: `opened = await openBrowserFn(authUrl.toString())` at `:210`; success `:211-212` prints only `'browser opened; complete authorization on the OpenRouter page'`; failure `:213-216` prints the manual-URL line. Timeout `:218-221` — no URL.
- `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_oauth_server.dart:9` imports `openBrowser` from `openrouter_oauth_server.dart`; `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow` (`:149`) takes `openBrowserFn = openBrowser` (`:151`), branches at `:172-177` (success `:173` `'browser opened; complete authorization with ChatGPT'` hides the URL; failure `:176` prints it). Timeout `:178-181` — no URL.
- Fourth family member, same shape: `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart` imports `openBrowser` at `:21`; `runAiinConnectCliFlow` (`:204`) takes `openBrowserFn` (`:206`); the branch lives at `:484-488` (success `:485` `'browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page'`, failure `:488` manual-URL line).
- Call sites: `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:145` (OpenRouter via `/provider`), `:161` (CodeMie SSO via `_mintCodeMieSsoCookie`, `:157`), `:1086` (OpenRouter re-login), `:1250-1298` (ChatGPT: `/provider chatgpt oauth [headless]` → `_handleChatGptOAuthCommand` `:1246` → `_runChatGptOAuthCommand` `:1257`, headless variant dispatched at `:1296`, interactive `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow` at `:1298`), `:1561` (CodeMie SSO recovery via `_handleCodeMieSsoCommand`, `:1551`).
- Precedent IN REPO that the target shape is not foreign: `_runChatGptHeadlessOAuth` (`lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:1322`) is a no-browser OAuth flow — it prints the instruction and the full URL (`io.writeln(authUrl.toString())`, `:1344`), then asks the user to paste the redirect URL. The card's core behavior already exists in the codebase for exactly one flow.
- No opt-out exists today: no `--no-browser` flag and no `FA_NO_BROWSER` env var anywhere in `lib/`, `bin/`, or `test/`. The only related env var is `FA_NO_FORMAT` (rendering only; `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart:280`, `lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart:1322`) — unrelated to browser launch.
- URL contents (threat-model input): CodeMie's URL is `<org base>/v1/auth/login/<port>` (`lib/src/providers/codemie_sso.dart:38-39`) — the localhost callback port is embedded; the token arrives later via the redirect to `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...` (`:36-37`) and is therefore never part of the printed URL. OpenRouter/ChatGPT URLs carry PKCE challenge + `state` + redirect URI.

**Positive/negative tests for the load-bearing fact** ("true ≠ opened"):
- Positive: with `openBrowserFn` stubbed to `async (u) => true`, the success branch must STILL print the full URL (this is the fix; today it does not — `test/cli/codemie_sso_server_test.dart:142` pins the old behavior).
- Negative: with the stub returning false, the URL line is…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. - **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1450` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +1602
- **Deletions**: -187
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T22:50:43Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T23:59:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1450
### What changed
Every CLI OAuth/SSO flow (OpenRouter, ChatGPT/Codex, CodeMie SSO, AIIN connect) now always prints a consistent, greppable `authorization URL: <url>` line, and a new `--no-browser` flag (plus a truthy `FA_NO_BROWSER` env var and a headless/remote auto-detect) skips the automatic browser launch — the URL stays on screen so the user can copy it into any browser and paste/redirect the callback back.

### Key decisions
- One shared launch step, `openAuthUrlWithStatus`, used by all four flows: prints skip/opened/could-not-open, then ALWAYS the URL line (also on timeout/failure — last-chance rescue) so the URL is never suppressed.
- New `shouldLaunchBrowser` policy in `openrouter_oauth_server.dart`: explicit `--no-browser` flag > `FA_NO_BROWSER` env > headless auto-detect (`TERM=dumb`, no `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` on Linux, SSH without display, non-TTY stdout).
- Flag threaded through `provider_commands` / per-provider command handlers into `runXxxCliFlow(shouldOpenBrowserFn: …)`; each flow keeps its `openBrowserFn` seam.
- AIIN connect now rides the configured `modelsHttpClient`, so the flow's exchange/key calls are testable without network.
- Command-layer end-to-end coverage in `agent_cli_oauth_no_browser_test.dart`: tests play the browser (read the printed URL, fire the real loopback callback) for OpenRouter, CodeMie, and AIIN; ChatGPT stays flow-test-only (its callback server binds pinned ports 1455/1457).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/agent_cli_oauth_no_browser_test.dart
dart test test/cli/browser_launch_policy_test.dart test/cli/openrouter_oauth_server_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_oauth_server_test.dart test/cli/codemie_sso_server_test.dart test/cli/aiin_connect_server_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Flow shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CMD["/provider … oauth|sso|connect --no-browser"] --> FLOW["runXxxCliFlow"]
  FLOOR["shouldLaunchBrowser: flag > FA_NO_BROWSER > headless detect"] --> FLOW
  FLOW -->|"false"| SKIP["prints: browser launch skipped"]
  FLOW -->|"true"| OPEN["openBrowserFn(url)"]
  SKIP --> URL
  OPEN --> URL["prints: authorization URL: <url>"]
  URL --> CB["loopback callback (user-driven)"]
  CB --> DONE["exchange / cookies → provider saved"]
```

</details>

# gh-1450: [GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)

## Description

[WIP][GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)

## Goal — the authorization URL is always visible and browser launch is always optional (v1)

One sentence: **OAuth/SSO login in fa becomes a flow where the full authorization URL is printed in every outcome and the automatic browser launch can be declined** — not a flow that hides the URL exactly when the launch command reports success.

Today all browser-driven login flows print the authorization URL only in the `openBrowser`-returned-false branch; in the success branch they print "browser opened" and nothing else. `openBrowser()` returns true merely because a launch command exited 0 — which says nothing about which browser, which profile, or whether a browser opened at all (SSH, headless, wrong default profile). A user for whom the default browser is the wrong destination gets a silent wait and a timeout that never reveals the URL. The fix is uniform: the URL is a first-class output line in BOTH branches, launch is skippable by flag, env, and headless auto-detect, and the timeout message carries the URL as a last-chance rescue.

## Why this framing

- **Retracted:** "the success branch is the happy path and needs no URL." That holds only when the default browser is the right destination. The incident shows the launch succeeding (exit 0) while being useless to the user — the URL was needed most precisely in the success branch.
- **Retracted:** "printing the URL always is redundant noise for interactive users." One extra status line per login is negligible; its absence is unrecoverable when the launch is wrong. Redundancy here is the safety property, not clutter.
- **Retracted (scope):** "fix CodeMie only — that is where the incident happened." OpenRouter and ChatGPT interactive flows share the identical branch shape through the same imported `openBrowser`; fixing one mechanism class means fixing all of them (AIIN is the fourth family member — see Capability surface).

## Incident (owner, 2026-10-09 — test data)

CodeMie SSO login in fa (`/provider` flow → `runCodeMieSsoCliFlow`, `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:161`). fa opened the auth link in the DEFAULT browser. The owner cannot authorize there (wrong browser/profile context), and the full URL was never printed, so he could not open it in the right browser himself. The flow waited and timed out. Owner quote: "оно открывает ссылку в дефолт браузере, а мне там не надо! я там не могу авторизовать, а ссылку оно полную не даёт".

Mechanism chain (each link pinned below):
(a) flow builds the URL and calls `openBrowserFn(ssoUrl)`;
(b) `openBrowser` shells out to `open`/`xdg-open`/`start` and reports "true when the launch command was invoked (not whether the browser actually opened)" — SSH/X-less sessions and wrong-default-profile sessions still report true;
(c) the true branch prints only "browser opened" — the URL is hidden exactly when the launch was attempted;
(d) the wait loop runs 5 minutes of "still waiting" statuses, then the timeout path returns without ever printing the URL — no self-rescue at any point.

Amplification: the success-branch design was self-confirming — every local, single-profile test session saw the browser open and the flow complete, so the missing URL line never surfaced as a failure. It survived until a multi-context user (remote machine / non-default browser profile) hit it, and even then the timeout made the failure look like a provider problem rather than a harness problem.

## Architecture (pinned facts, re-verified against the working tree)

The three interactive flows share one shape — an injectable `openBrowserFn` seam defaulting to the shared `openBrowser`, a branch on its boolean, and a timeout path:

```
runXxxCliFlow
  ├─ build <authUrl>  (callback port + state embedded; token never part of the URL)
  ├─ openBrowserFn(authUrl) ──true──▶ onStatus('browser opened; …')   ← URL HIDDEN
  │                        └─false─▶ onStatus('open this URL manually: $url')  ← only rescue line today
  ├─ wait for localhost callback (5 min, periodic 'still waiting')
  └─ timeout ─▶ onStatus('no … received (timeout or cancelled)')      ← URL HIDDEN
```

- `lib/src/cli/codemie_sso_server.dart:75` `runCodeMieSsoCliFlow` starts the callback server, builds `ssoUrl` (`:82`), branches at `:84-89`: success prints only `'browser opened; complete the CodeMie sign-in'` (`:85`); failure prints `'could not open browser automatically'` (`:87`) and `'open this URL manually: $ssoUrl'` (`:88`). Wait loop `:90-107`: `const wait = Duration(minutes: 5)` (`:98`), periodic "still waiting" every 15 s (`:99-101`), `server.waitForToken().timeout(wait)` (`:103`). Timeout branch `:108-110` prints `'no SSO callback received (timeout or cancelled)'` — no URL.
- `lib/src/cli/openrouter_oauth_server.dart:157-178` `openBrowser` (doc `:152-156`): `open` (macOS) / `xdg-open` (Linux) / `start` (Windows), returns `result.exitCode == 0`; unsupported platform and thrown launch errors return false. Doc comment admits: "Returns true when the launch command was invoked (not whether the browser actually opened)."
- `lib/src/cli/openrouter_oauth_server.dart:185` `runOpenRouterOAuthCliFlow`: `opened = await openBrowserFn(authUrl.toString())` at `:210`; success `:211-212` prints only `'browser opened; complete authorization on the OpenRouter page'`; failure `:213-216` prints the manual-URL line. Timeout `:218-221` — no URL.
- `lib/src/cli/chatgpt_oauth_server.dart:9` imports `openBrowser` from `openrouter_oauth_server.dart`; `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow` (`:149`) takes `openBrowserFn = openBrowser` (`:151`), branches at `:172-177` (success `:173` `'browser opened; complete authorization with ChatGPT'` hides the URL; failure `:176` prints it). Timeout `:178-181` — no URL.
- Fourth family member, same shape: `lib/src/cli/aiin_connect_server.dart` imports `openBrowser` at `:21`; `runAiinConnectCliFlow` (`:204`) takes `openBrowserFn` (`:206`); the branch lives at `:484-488` (success `:485` `'browser opened; sign in on the AIIN page'`, failure `:488` manual-URL line).
- Call sites: `lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:145` (OpenRouter via `/provider`), `:161` (CodeMie SSO via `_mintCodeMieSsoCookie`, `:157`), `:1086` (OpenRouter re-login), `:1250-1298` (ChatGPT: `/provider chatgpt oauth [headless]` → `_handleChatGptOAuthCommand` `:1246` → `_runChatGptOAuthCommand` `:1257`, headless variant dispatched at `:1296`, interactive `runChatGptOAuthCliFlow` at `:1298`), `:1561` (CodeMie SSO recovery via `_handleCodeMieSsoCommand`, `:1551`).
- Precedent IN REPO that the target shape is not foreign: `_runChatGptHeadlessOAuth` (`lib/src/cli/provider_commands.dart:1322`) is a no-browser OAuth flow — it prints the instruction and the full URL (`io.writeln(authUrl.toString())`, `:1344`), then asks the user to paste the redirect URL. The card's core behavior already exists in the codebase for exactly one flow.
- No opt-out exists today: no `--no-browser` flag and no `FA_NO_BROWSER` env var anywhere in `lib/`, `bin/`, or `test/`. The only related env var is `FA_NO_FORMAT` (rendering only; `lib/src/cli/cli_args.dart:280`, `lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart:1322`) — unrelated to browser launch.
- URL contents (threat-model input): CodeMie's URL is `<org base>/v1/auth/login/<port>` (`lib/src/providers/codemie_sso.dart:38-39`) — the localhost callback port is embedded; the token arrives later via the redirect to `http://localhost:<port>/?token=...` (`:36-37`) and is therefore never part of the printed URL. OpenRouter/ChatGPT URLs carry PKCE challenge + `state` + redirect URI.

**Positive/negative tests for the load-bearing fact** ("true ≠ opened"):
- Positive: with `openBrowserFn` stubbed to `async (u) => true`, the success branch must STILL print the full URL (this is the fix; today it does not — `test/cli/codemie_sso_server_test.dart:142` pins the old behavior).
- Negative: with the stub returning false, the URL line is…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1464
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1464
- **Title**: gh-1450 [GOAL] SSO/OAuth login must always show the full authorization URL and allow opting out of the default browser (CodeMie/OpenRouter/ChatGPT family)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1450` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 21
- **Additions**: +1602
- **Deletions**: -187
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T22:50:43Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T23:59:46Z

## PR Description

Closes #1450
### What changed
Every CLI OAuth/SSO flow (OpenRouter, ChatGPT/Codex, CodeMie SSO, AIIN connect) now always prints a consistent, greppable `authorization URL: <url>` line, and a new `--no-browser` flag (plus a truthy `FA_NO_BROWSER` env var and a headless/remote auto-detect) skips the automatic browser launch — the URL stays on screen so the user can copy it into any browser and paste/redirect the callback back.

### Key decisions
- One shared launch step, `openAuthUrlWithStatus`, used by all four flows: prints skip/opened/could-not-open, then ALWAYS the URL line (also on timeout/failure — last-chance rescue) so the URL is never suppressed.
- New `shouldLaunchBrowser` policy in `openrouter_oauth_server.dart`: explicit `--no-browser` flag > `FA_NO_BROWSER` env > headless auto-detect (`TERM=dumb`, no `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` on Linux, SSH without display, non-TTY stdout).
- Flag threaded through `provider_commands` / per-provider command handlers into `runXxxCliFlow(shouldOpenBrowserFn: …)`; each flow keeps its `openBrowserFn` seam.
- AIIN connect now rides the configured `modelsHttpClient`, so the flow's exchange/key calls are testable without network.
- Command-layer end-to-end coverage in `agent_cli_oauth_no_browser_test.dart`: tests play the browser (read the printed URL, fire the real loopback callback) for OpenRouter, CodeMie, and AIIN; ChatGPT stays flow-test-only (its callback server binds pinned ports 1455/1457).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/agent_cli_oauth_no_browser_test.dart
dart test test/cli/browser_launch_policy_test.dart test/cli/openrouter_oauth_server_test.dart test/cli/chatgpt_oauth_server_test.dart test/cli/codemie_sso_server_test.dart test/cli/aiin_connect_server_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Flow shape</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CMD["/provider … oauth|sso|connect --no-browser"] --> FLOW["runXxxCliFlow"]
  FLOOR["shouldLaunchBrowser: flag > FA_NO_BROWSER > headless detect"] --> FLOW
  FLOW -->|"false"| SKIP["prints: browser launch skipped"]
  FLOW -->|"true"| OPEN["openBrowserFn(url)"]
  SKIP --> URL
  OPEN --> URL["prints: authorization URL: <url>"]
  URL --> CB["loopback callback (user-driven)"]
  CB --> DONE["exchange / cookies → provider saved"]
```

</details>
